observations.reason: Standalone Vulkan allocation reproduction and native heap diagnostic attribution, not a rendering benchmark.

report.finding:
Native heap sampling on the profileable releaseAPK (unchanged d7e154213 native library) attributes approximately1.32GB of live sampled allocations to vkAllocateCommandBuffers through Mali create_command_buffer_builder. The trace has no heap-sampling overrun/error counters; sampling overhead excludes timing acceptance. Android settledPSS was1,650,719KiB.

A standalone Vulkan C reproduction, with no Cherenkov/wgpu code, allocates2640primary command buffers from a TRANSIENT pool. malloc-used changes1,242,704→1,182,042,720B; ordinary reset and RESET_RELEASE_RESOURCES retain it. vkFreeCommandBuffers reduces it to1,288,736B and RSS191,312→31,024KiB. This is retained command-buffer allocation, not a demonstrated driver leak.

The locked wgpu Vulkan HAL retains completed command buffers in its encoder pool; each renderpass also opens underlying command buffers. Picture/mip passes therefore expose a substantial command-memory cost beyond texture residency. A proper idle reclamation path is being evaluated; no dependency code has been modified.
